newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks millions in seed money for DC roads.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks millions in seed money for DC roads.

text.p: The White House proposed on Tuesday that Congress appropriate $125 million in fiscal year 1998 to help the District of Columbia rebuild crumbling roads, bridges and other transportation infrastructure.

Seed money from the Federal Highway Trust Fund would be reallocated to a proposed National Capital Infrastructure Fund, the Administration said in announcing a broad $3.9 billion, five-year federal aid plan for the District of Columbia.

The new authority could use seed money to construct local roads and bridges, to pay the local match for road and bridge projects financed with federal aid, and to pay capital expenditures for the Washington Metropolitant Area Transit Authority, the White House plan says.
Funds would be available only for capital projects, the White House said, adding that routine maintenance projects would not be eligible.
The President's plan says the new fund could accept contributions from other sources, like universities, hospitals amd other tax-exempt organziations.
